comparison: Both evaluate the discovery of FipA-FlhF interaction (C21-C27, C3-C4) and find it SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the convergence of co-IP-MS/MS and BACTH methods, while peer reviewers highlight the unbiased discovery approach and convincing biochemical/genetic demonstration. Both accept the interaction data without concerns.

OpenEval R1 includes cross-species validation (C36-C38) which peer R3 also addresses. Both find the conservation of FipA-FlhF interaction across P. putida and S. putrefaciens SUPPORTED, with peer reviewers noting species-specific nuances are valid findings.

Perfect overlap on FipA characterization claims (C28-C35). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the causal relationship between FipA presence and polar flagellation is inferred rather than experimentally demonstrated, while peer reviewers accept the phylogenetic and structural characterization without critique.

Both address V. parahaemolyticus phenotypic characterization (C39-C44) and find it SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes data consistency and appropriate controls, while peer reviewers note the comprehensive and convincing nature of the mutant analysis.

OpenEval R3 includes cross-species phenotypic data (C81-C85) which peer R5 addresses. Both find SUPPORTED with acknowledgment of species-specific differences. Peer reviewers note presentation clarity as a weakness but do not question data validity.

Both evaluate FipA's role in FlhF localization in V. parahaemolyticus (C45-C50) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights protein stability controls, while peer reviewers accept the localization data and interpretation without critique.

Both address the additive effect of fipA and hubP deletions (C51-C54) and find it SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes this supports independent pathways, while peer reviewers explicitly note FipA facilitates FlhF recruitment together with HubP.

OpenEval R4 includes cross-species FlhF localization data (C86-C93) which peer R8 addresses. Both find SUPPORTED with acknowledgment of species-specific differences. Peer reviewers note the comparison is challenging to readers but do not question validity.

Perfect overlap on transmembrane domain requirement (C55-C58, C94). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the E. coli topology mapping may not perfectly reflect native topology, while peer reviewers accept the comprehensive domain analysis without critique.

Both address conserved residue identification and FlhF interaction interface (C59-C64, C95, C111-C112) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes separation of interaction interfaces, while peer reviewers confirm the DUF2802 domain mediates FipA-FlhF interaction.

Both evaluate functional importance of DUF2802 domain (C65-C69, C113) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights consistency across assays, while peer reviewers confirm the domain is required for FipA function through comprehensive analysis.

Perfect overlap on FipA localization dynamics (C70-C76, C96-C100). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the inference about FipA appearing before flagellar synthesis is based on timing correlations, while peer reviewers explicitly accept the time-series analysis showing FipA localizes prior to or coincident with flagellar assembly.

Both address FlhF-dependent FipA localization across species (C77-C80, C101-C106, C121-C122) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes limited protein stability controls, while peer reviewers accept the localization dependencies as demonstrated.

Both evaluate S. putrefaciens-specific HubP role (C107-C108, C123-C124) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval documents species-specific differences, while peer reviewers accept these as valid findings reflecting evolutionary nuances.

Both address the functional model of FipA's role (C110, C114, C119-C120) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes direct biochemical evidence for FlhF activation is lacking, while peer reviewers call this a significant contribution and find the mechanistic model convincing.

Perfect overlap on differential effects of fipA vs hubP deletions (C115-C118). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval suggests time-lapse experiments would strengthen conclusions, while peer reviewers accept the demonstration of two distinct pathways.

Perfect overlap on speculative mechanistic models (C128-C129, C131). OpenEval evaluates as UNCERTAIN noting these are hypotheses requiring validation, while peer reviewers evaluate as SUPPORTED, accepting them as reasonable interpretations that open avenues for further research.

Near-perfect overlap on background knowledge claims (C1, C9-C20, C23, C125-C126, C130). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes these are appropriately referenced prior findings, while peer reviewers accept the established facts without question.

OpenEval R13 addresses knowledge gaps (C2, C127) as SUPPORTED statements of what remains unknown. Peer R18 includes C2 among background claims, also evaluating as SUPPORTED. Both accept these frame the scope appropriately.
